title: Joseph’s brothers once threw him into a pit.
paragraphs: Joseph’s brothers once threw him into a pit.

They stripped him of his robe.
They sold him into slavery.
They told their father he was gone forever.
For years Joseph carried the scars of betrayal.

He became a slave in a foreign land.
He was falsely accused.
He was thrown into prison.
Most people would have carried bitterness for the rest of their lives.
But Joseph carried something different.
He carried perspective.
Years later, when famine struck the land, Joseph stood as the second most powerful man in Egypt.
And one day the unthinkable happened.
The very brothers who betrayed him walked into the room.
They didn’t recognize him.
But Joseph recognized them.
Imagine that moment.

The men who sold you…
standing helpless before you.

Joseph had the power to imprison them.
The power to punish them.
The power to make them feel the pain they once caused.
But Joseph chose something far greater.
He chose forgiveness.
And he said one of the most powerful lines in the entire Bible:
“You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good.”
Joseph understood something many people never realize.
God can take betrayal and turn it into positioning.
God can take rejection and turn it into preparation.
God can take the pit and turn it into a palace.
Joseph refused to let bitterness rewrite his story.
Because when you truly trust God’s sovereignty, you no longer see people as the authors of your pain.
You see God as the author of your purpose.
And sometimes the greatest freedom in your life begins the moment you release the people who hurt you.
